lines.text: She says his love is more delightful than wine and hopes the king will bring her to his chambers.
She says she is dark like the tents of Kedar, and her mother's sons made her keeper of the vineyards.
He compares her to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots, and they promise ornaments of gold studded with beads of silver.
She calls her beloved a sachet of myrrh and a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of Lebanon.
She delights to sit in his shade, and she tells the daughters of Samaria not to awaken love until the time is right.
